judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The postal-code input is wrapped in an empty <label> and has only placeholder='Código postal'. The capture's Chrome CDP tree gives it role textbox with no name, so the claim is true of the capture. The skeptic's point: HTML-AAM's input name computation says 'If the accessible name is still empty ... use the value of the control's placeholder attribute', and ACT rule e086e5 (Passed Example 5) treats a placeholder as enough for a non-empty accessible name. By the spec, the field's name is 'Código postal', and Chrome's empty result after the empty label looks like a user-agent quirk. Users of Chrome still get no name exposed. Whether that is an authoring failure of 4.1.2 is something competent auditors would disagree on. The live server HTML has the identical markup.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: 'Ver tudo' under CALÇADOS > Masculino (/calcados/masculino/adulto). The CALÇADOS list holds four 'Ver tudo' links (women's, men's, boys', girls' shoes) under the same parent item. The snapshot has 28 'Ver tudo' links with 28 distinct hrefs, so the claim holds of the capture. The link is in the 'seoMenuNav' copy of the menu. Live Menu.min.css gives .seoMenuItem/.seoSubMenuItem height:0 and .seoSubMenuLink font-size:0; line-height:0, so sighted users never see it, but it is in the accessibility tree and focusable. That copy is a flat list: the column labels ('Feminino', 'Masculino', 'Plus Size') are sibling list items, not headings, so by this rubric's context list the only context is the parent list item, which these same-name links share, and they lead to non-equivalent listings. Whether that fails 2.4.4 depends on R1's 'visual information' clause, and R1 does not cover links nobody can see. Read literally, nothing visible tells this pair apart, so the pair meets the expectation (no). But the visible mega-menu (hover-rendered; the CSS has SubMenuList/SubMenuBannerImg) very likely shows the same links under visible column titles. If so, the purpose is clear to sighted users and only assistive-technology users get the ambiguous copies, which is not 'ambiguous to users in general'. The capture has no hover state to confirm the visible dropdown. Competent auditors would split on this, so the label is uncertain. The live server HTML has the same 28 links.
